card.name: Linking words before electrolyte-disorder terms
card.fires_on: Small linking words such as "of", "to", "for" and "and" right after "risk", "lead" or an electrolyte disorder name. The next word is expected to be a mineral or metabolic problem such as hypercalcemia, hyperkalemia or acidosis.

modes.label: Risk of ...
modes.description: "of" or "for" after "increase the risk" in interaction warnings, before a metabolic or electrolyte problem.
modes.example: Potassium phosphates injection may increase the risk<< of>> hyperkalemia, including life-threatening

modes.label: Lead to ...
modes.description: "to" after "may lead" where serum abnormalities are expected next.
modes.example: High intake of calcium and phosphate concomitant with vitamin D compounds may lead<< to>> serum abnormalities requiring more frequent patient monitoring and

modes.label: Paired disorders
modes.description: "and" joining two electrolyte disorders in a warning heading.
modes.example: Hyperphosphatemia<< and>> Hypocalcemia : Monitor serum phosph

card.writes: It seems to prepare the model to write an electrolyte or metabolic disorder term next, while discouraging unrelated words.
card.plain: It fires on the small word just before a warning names a mineral or acid-base problem, like "risk of" hypercalcemia.
